label: Table 12.1
caption: Table 12.1 Limitations on roof coverings
description:
Table 12.1 “Limitations on roof coverings” is a grid. The left-hand column is headed “Designation(1) of covering of roof or part of roof”. The four columns to its right are grouped under the heading “Distance from any point on relevant boundary” and are headed, from left to right, “Less than 6m”, “At least 6m”, “At least 12m” and “At least 20m”. The row labels are shown as B, C, D, E and F, each with a subscript “ROOF(t4)”.

The extracted text has lost the symbols that show acceptance. Visually, the table uses a solid black circle to mean acceptable and an open circle to mean not acceptable. The key beneath the grid gives the exact words: “● Acceptable.” and “○ Not acceptable.”

Reading the grid row by row: in the B row with subscript ROOF(t4), all four distance columns contain a solid black circle. In the C row with subscript ROOF(t4), the “Less than 6m” column contains an open circle, and the “At least 6m”, “At least 12m” and “At least 20m” columns each contain a solid black circle. In the D row with subscript ROOF(t4), “Less than 6m” contains an open circle; “At least 6m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)(3)”; “At least 12m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)”; and “At least 20m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)”. In the E row with subscript ROOF(t4), “Less than 6m” contains an open circle; “At least 6m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)(3)”; “At least 12m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)(3)”; and “At least 20m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)”. In the F row with subscript ROOF(t4), “Less than 6m”, “At least 6m” and “At least 12m” each contain an open circle, and “At least 20m” contains a solid black circle with the superscript “(2)(3)”.

There is no drawing inside the table. The title band is shaded green, but the heading row and the data cells are not shaded; the key uses the two circle symbols, not shading.

The notes beneath the table, in the table’s words, are: “Separation distances do not apply to the boundary between roofs of a pair of semi-detached dwellinghouses and to enclosed/covered walkways. However, see Diagram 5.2 if the roof passes over the top of a compartment wall. Polycarbonate and uPVC rooflights that achieve a class C-s3, d2 rating by test may be regarded as having a B_ROOF(t4) designation. 1. The designation of external roof surfaces is explained in Appendix B. 2. Not acceptable on any of the following buildings. a. Dwellinghouses in terraces of three or more dwellinghouses. b. Any other buildings with a cubic capacity of more than 1500m3. 3. Acceptable on buildings not listed in (2) if both of the following apply. a. Part of the roof has a maximum area of 3m2 and is a minimum of 1500mm from any similar part. b. The roof between the parts is covered with a material rated class A2-s3, d2 or better.”
